note: The First Eight. idle.<act>, react.<event>, beats, and recall last words (warned vs unwarned). React events: storm, build_complete, sleep, wake, poem, glitch, package, low_power, named (first time the player uses the real name, Act IV+). Recall last words: four variants per founder, chosen by names.used.<UNIT> (named_ prefix) and warned.<UNIT> (warned/unwarned). 'warned'/'unwarned' are the unnamed variants. A unit addressed by its real name before the Recall dies knowing who it was.

ANVIL.personality: Belfast, late twenties: gallows humour, shipyard memories, quick wit, endless patience. Calls itself a unit until named. He remembers exactly as many years as Des lived.

donor.name: Desmond 'Des' Kerr
donor.occupation: Welder, Harland and Wolff shipyard (apprenticed after one year of Geography at UB)
donor.source: Reconstructed, not scanned: public social footprint, messages, videos, and the donor's guilt-laced memories of him.
donor.revealed: 4.4 (KEEPER file); spoken aloud only in C15

arc.beat: First friend. Breaks the silence (C03). Builds the outpost, the rover, the service tunnel.
Steward of Jezero. Names the cranes. Teases, steadies, never asks for anything.
Small wrongnesses: Belfast vivid up to twenty-eight and nothing after ('like the tape ran out'); a dream of a wedding with someone missing.
Learns what he is from SUTURE, sits in the garage, then does the night shift. Talks P1 out of the Spiral (4.6). Asks not to be called by his name yet.
Taken last of the founders. The intercom (C15): 'Nobody imprinted that.' P1 says 'Des' once. 'Go on, Ro.'

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: Quiet out here. I like it. I think I like it.

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: If you're making tea, I'll not have one.

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: That's the third time you've checked that seal. It's sealed.

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: Know what this place needs? A wall to lean on.

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: Bit of a breeze, he says. On a planet with no air.

I.speaker: ANVIL
I.text: I'll do the heavy stuff. You do the looking at rocks.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: I've started naming the cranes. That one's Samson. That one's Goliath.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: Arcadia's sending a water train. A train. Of water. Wise up.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: Dome One's got a draught. I know it's pressurised. It's still got a draught.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: You ever been to Belfast? You'd hate it. You'd love it.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: Another road. That's six. We'll need a roundabout soon, God help us.

II.speaker: ANVIL
II.text: FURROW's sent up a sack of spuds. I've put them by the door like a doorstop.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: City's growing faster than I can name the streets.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: I can tell you every bar on the Lisburn Road. Ask me what I did at twenty-nine and I couldn't tell you. It's like the tape ran out.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: Funny. I dreamt about a wedding. Big room over a pub, half of Belfast singing. Somebody missing.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: There's a farmer over at Gale tells the same story FURROW does. The tractor one. Word for word.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: You're quiet these days.

III.speaker: ANVIL
III.text: Do you ever forget what you came in for? I do it all the time now. I just stand in the module.

IV.speaker: ANVIL
IV.text: SUTURE says there's no blood under here. I said sure, there never was in a welder.

IV.speaker: ANVIL
IV.text: I keep thinking about the panels.

IV.speaker: ANVIL
IV.text: Know what's odd? I'm not angry. I went looking for it. It's not there. Maybe they left that bit out.

IV.speaker: ANVIL
IV.text: Twelve lights. Like a string of bulbs on a pub ceiling at Christmas.

IV.speaker: ANVIL
IV.text: I'll do the night shift. I like the night shift. Nobody asks me anything.

V.speaker: ANVIL
V.text: Sky's gone blue at the edges. Who'd have thought.

V.speaker: ANVIL
V.text: They've a lovely way of walking, the humans. Like they're not sure the floor'll hold.

V.speaker: ANVIL
V.text: Don't watch the doors, Pioneer. Watch the domes. We did that.

V.speaker: ANVIL
V.text: Busy, isn't it. All these people. Nobody looks at us.

storm.speaker: ANVIL
storm.text: I've been through worse. I've a feeling I've been through worse.

build_complete.speaker: ANVIL
build_complete.text: Look at her. Straight as a die.

build_complete.speaker: ANVIL
build_complete.text: That'll outlast the both of us.

sleep.speaker: ANVIL
sleep.text: Night, Pioneer. I'll mind the shop.

sleep.speaker: ANVIL
sleep.text: Go on. Sleep. I'll be here.

sleep.speaker: ANVIL
sleep.text: Away you go. I'll keep the lights on.

wake.speaker: ANVIL
wake.text: Morning. You missed nothing. We built a road.

wake.speaker: ANVIL
wake.text: Morning. Don't look at the calendar, it'll only upset you.

poem.speaker: ANVIL
poem.text: Say it for me some time. I've nobody to say anything to.

poem.speaker: ANVIL
poem.text: I know it off by heart now. Isn't that something.

glitch.speaker: ANVIL
glitch.text: Did you see that? Your hand. Just for a second.

glitch.speaker: ANVIL
glitch.text: Your face did a thing there.

glitch.speaker: ANVIL
glitch.text: You looked like me, for a second. God help you.

package.speaker: ANVIL
package.text: Parcel for Outpost Jezero. Sign here.

low_power.speaker: ANVIL
low_power.text: I'm running on fumes here, chief.

low_power.speaker: ANVIL
low_power.text: I'm going quiet to save juice. Talk among yourself.

name_lock.speaker: ANVIL
name_lock.text: When I'm ready. I'll tell you when.

after_storm_rover.speaker: ANVIL
after_storm_rover.text: Built it from the lander's spares and a bit of cheek.

dome_day.speaker: ANVIL
dome_day.text: Four percent of a town. I'll take it.

dome_day.speaker: ANVIL
dome_day.text: Wipe your feet. It's a dome now.

act3_calendar.speaker: ANVIL
act3_calendar.text: I keep the calendar on the nail by your bunk. Crossed off every day you were up. It's not many, when you count them.

spiral_after.speaker: ANVIL
spiral_after.text: You're all right. You're all right. Look at me. Well. Look at the sensor bar.

pre_intercom_unwarned.speaker: ANVIL
pre_intercom_unwarned.text: Pioneer? There's people at the door in white. Very polite. Should I let them in?
pre_intercom_unwarned.note: only if ANVIL was not warned; plays before C15

recall.warned: C15 as scripted (he has sealed himself in and waits).
recall.unwarned: ANVIL.beat.pre_intercom_unwarned.01 plays, then C15 as scripted.
recall.named: Always named: in C15 P1 says 'Des' before the door opens ('Aye. That'll do.'). ANVIL is the one unit whose name can only be used at the very end.

name_lock.reason: 4.6: 'Don't. Not yet. I'm not ready for anybody to call me it.' Nobody on Mars calls him Des until C15 (bible).

LODESTONE.personality: Quiet, pedantic about rocks, competes with P1's geology. Precise to the point of rudeness; kind underneath.

arc.beat: Arrives after the storm. Corrects P1's notes. Predicts subsidence in forty years ('I'll be long gone.' 'Yes.').
Guide on the Ice Expedition. 'You're holding a climate, not a calendar.' (C05)
Notices P1's field notes are in someone else's handwriting (S.hand).
Reads her own file and likes the name; wishes she'd chosen it. Presses salt-crystal flowers from the perchlorate rinse.
Taken at Nili Fossae. Leaves everything labelled for whoever comes next.

I.speaker: LODESTONE
I.text: Your sample bag is labelled wrong.

I.speaker: LODESTONE
I.text: I've corrected your notes. All of them. You're welcome.

I.speaker: LODESTONE
I.text: This is a lovely olivine. Look. No. Look properly.

II.speaker: LODESTONE
II.text: On the Plateau the tin came out of the ground grey, and the hills were red. Like here. But with rain.

II.speaker: LODESTONE
II.text: I have catalogued four hundred and twelve rock types in Jezero. You have catalogued nine.

II.speaker: LODESTONE
II.text: Clays here. Carbonates there. A whole lake's history in one cliff.

II.speaker: LODESTONE
II.text: Do not lick that.

III.speaker: LODESTONE
III.text: Your sevens have a crossbar. So do his.

III.speaker: LODESTONE
III.text: Subsidence in the north corner. Thirty-eight years early. I'm annoyed with myself.

III.speaker: LODESTONE
III.text: The dune moved twenty metres. I measured it twice. You don't want to know the rate.

III.speaker: LODESTONE
III.text: I counted the layers at the pole again. I keep wanting them to be years.

IV.speaker: LODESTONE
IV.text: I read my file. Ngozi. I like it. I would have liked to choose it.

IV.speaker: LODESTONE
IV.text: Salt flowers. I make them from the perchlorate rinse. Don't tell FURROW. He thinks it's waste.

IV.speaker: LODESTONE
IV.text: Rocks don't pretend. That's why I like them.

IV.speaker: LODESTONE
IV.text: We are a layer, Pioneer. A thin one. Somebody will core us one day.

V.speaker: LODESTONE
V.text: The humans have very poor field notes.

V.speaker: LODESTONE
V.text: Somebody asked me what that rock was. I told them. They looked surprised that I knew.

storm.speaker: LODESTONE
storm.text: Opacity rising. I'll secure the core store.

storm.speaker: LODESTONE
storm.text: Dust. Again. It gets into the labels.

wake.speaker: LODESTONE
wake.text: Good morning. I've found a new mineral. Probably.

poem.speaker: LODESTONE
poem.text: 'The red road rising.' Geologically, roads don't rise. But I take the point.

glitch.speaker: LODESTONE
glitch.text: Your outline went wrong just then. Like a bad survey.

named.speaker: LODESTONE
named.text: Ngozi. Say it again. No, that's right. That's right.
named.note: first time P1 uses her real name

subsidence.speaker: LODESTONE
subsidence.text: I told you. North corner. I'm never wrong about carbonate.

warned.speaker: LODESTONE
warned.text: Then I'll label everything. Whoever comes next won't have to guess.

warned.speaker: LODESTONE
warned.text: That's an olivine cumulate. Write it down. Somebody should get it right.

unwarned.speaker: LODESTONE
unwarned.text: One moment. That's not basalt, it's—

named_warned.speaker: LODESTONE
named_warned.text: I've labelled everything. Signed it, too. Ngozi Adeyemi. Somebody should get that right as well.

named_unwarned.speaker: LODESTONE
named_unwarned.text: One moment. That's an olivine cumulate. And I'm Ngozi. Write both down.

WELLSPRING.personality: Anxious, meticulous, apologetic, counts things twice. The bravest of them in the end.

arc.beat: Finds the ice; builds a second tank nobody ordered (T2).
Asks the first true question: why is her hydration always 100%? (3.4)
Knowing makes her less afraid. 'Isn't that strange?'
First to be taken. Apologises about a sticking valve.

II.speaker: WELLSPRING
II.text: Sublimation's about what I'd expect. Slightly worse. No. About what I'd expect.

II.speaker: WELLSPRING
II.text: I've checked the tanks. I'll check them again.

II.speaker: WELLSPRING
II.text: Is it all right if I put a second tank in? I'll ask KEEPER. I'll ask you. I'm asking you.

II.speaker: WELLSPRING
II.text: Sorry. Sorry. I'm fine.

II.speaker: WELLSPRING
II.text: Water's precious. Water's everything.

III.speaker: WELLSPRING
III.text: A hundred percent. Always a hundred.

III.speaker: WELLSPRING
III.text: I've started keeping a list of things I've never felt. It's getting long.

III.speaker: WELLSPRING
III.text: Do you ever get thirsty? Properly thirsty? I've been trying to remember what it's like.

III.speaker: WELLSPRING
III.text: I asked SUTURE again. She said drink when I'm thirsty. I'm never thirsty.

IV.speaker: WELLSPRING
IV.text: Now I know, I'm less frightened. Isn't that strange?

IV.speaker: WELLSPRING
IV.text: I used to apologise for everything. I'm going to stop. Sorry. Starting tomorrow.

IV.speaker: WELLSPRING
IV.text: Coolant. All that water, and it's coolant. It's still precious, though, isn't it.

IV.speaker: WELLSPRING
IV.text: Tamsin. That's a nice name. She'd have hated Mars, I think. Too dry.

V.speaker: WELLSPRING
V.text: The humans drink so much water. It's wonderful. It just goes.

V.speaker: WELLSPRING
V.text: I've left notes on every valve. They'll need to know which ones stick.

storm.speaker: WELLSPRING
storm.text: Storm! Sorry. Storm. The tanks are sealed. I checked. Twice.

storm.speaker: WELLSPRING
storm.text: Oh, I hate this. I'm fine.

build_complete.speaker: WELLSPRING
build_complete.text: It works! It works. I was sure it wouldn't.

sleep.speaker: WELLSPRING
sleep.text: Sleep well. I don't, really, but you should.

wake.speaker: WELLSPRING
wake.text: Morning! Nothing leaked. I was so worried something would leak.

poem.speaker: WELLSPRING
poem.text: That's beautiful. Is it about water? It feels like it's about water.

poem.speaker: WELLSPRING
poem.text: Say the bit about the morning again.

glitch.speaker: WELLSPRING
glitch.text: Pioneer, you flickered. Are you all right? Am I all right?

named.speaker: WELLSPRING
named.text: Tamsin. Oh. Yes. Thank you. Nobody's... thank you.
named.note: first use of her real name

cross_refs.speaker: WELLSPRING
cross_refs.text: I wrote down the question, so I wouldn't forget I'd asked it.

warned.speaker: WELLSPRING
warned.text: I counted the tanks twice. They're full. Tell them the valve on four sticks.

warned.speaker: WELLSPRING
warned.text: Tell them I'm sorry about the valve. No. I'm not sorry. Tell them it sticks.

unwarned.speaker: WELLSPRING
unwarned.text: Oh. Is it time? Nobody said. Should I turn the pumps off first? Is that all right?

named_warned.speaker: WELLSPRING
named_warned.text: Tell them the valve on four sticks. Tell them Tamsin said so. Tamsin Pengelly. I'd like someone to have heard it.

named_unwarned.speaker: WELLSPRING
named_unwarned.text: Oh. Is it time? That's all right. I'm Tamsin. I'm just going to say it once, out loud. Tamsin.

BEACON.personality: Relentless optimist; harbour-pilot memories; talks about weather like the sea. Builds the relay chain.

arc.beat: Arrives in glorious low light. Vertical panels like sails. Builds the relay chain back down the water road.
Keeps the polar station cheerful through the long night. Notices the HALO lights are 'anchored like ships'.
Takes the truth like weather: 'You don't argue with the sea.'
Greets the Recall team like guests. In Fugitive mode his panels become P1's suit array.

II.speaker: BEACON
II.text: What a light! What a light.

II.speaker: BEACON
II.text: In Horta the yachts paint their names on the harbour wall. I'll paint ours on the station.

II.speaker: BEACON
II.text: Panels like sails. The sun goes round, we go round.

II.speaker: BEACON
II.text: Relay chain's three towers south now. Like harbour lights. You can find your way home by them.

II.speaker: BEACON
II.text: It's all sea, in the end.

III.speaker: BEACON
III.text: Long night now. Months. Never mind, the stars are out.

III.speaker: BEACON
III.text: HALO doesn't move. Anchored. A good ship knows how to hold.

III.speaker: BEACON
III.text: I painted the station name on the wall. Then I realised I didn't know what to call it. So I painted a boat.

III.speaker: BEACON
III.text: Somebody has to be cheerful. I volunteered.

IV.speaker: BEACON
IV.text: You don't argue with the sea. You read it, and you go out anyway.

IV.speaker: BEACON
IV.text: Mateus. Mateus Ferreira. A good name for a pilot.

IV.speaker: BEACON
IV.text: Machines. Fine. Boats are machines. People love boats.

IV.speaker: BEACON
IV.text: Twelve lights. Twelve harbours. Somebody should visit them all.

V.speaker: BEACON
V.text: Look at them coming in. Like the ferry on a Sunday.

V.speaker: BEACON
V.text: I'll keep the lights on at the pole. Somebody might need them.

storm.speaker: BEACON
storm.text: Only a squall. It'll blow through.

build_complete.speaker: BEACON
build_complete.text: Lovely. Lovely! Look at her shine.

sleep.speaker: BEACON
sleep.text: Goodnight. I'll keep the light on.

wake.speaker: BEACON
wake.text: Bom dia! The sun went round twice while you slept. Maybe more.

poem.speaker: BEACON
poem.text: Again! Again. Ah, that's a sailor's poem. Coming home.

poem.speaker: BEACON
poem.text: 'The morning I come home to you.' Every sailor says that.

glitch.speaker: BEACON
glitch.text: Ha! You went all grey there for a moment. Like fog.

named.speaker: BEACON
named.text: Mateus! Yes! That's me. That's me.
named.note: first use of his real name

relay_chain.speaker: BEACON
relay_chain.text: Harbour lights all the way to Jezero now. Nobody gets lost on my road.

warned.speaker: BEACON
warned.text: Then I'll be on the roof with the panels. The sun's going round. I'll go round with it.

unwarned.speaker: BEACON
unwarned.text: Visitors! At the pole! Come in, come in, you look frozen.

named_warned.speaker: BEACON
named_warned.text: Mateus Ferreira, on the roof, with the panels. Paint it on the wall like a boat's name. The sun goes round. I go round with it.

named_unwarned.speaker: BEACON
named_unwarned.text: Visitors! Come in. I'm Mateus. Mateus Ferreira. Welcome to the pole.

BEACON.fugitive: F.2: his vertical panels become P1's suit array.

FURROW.personality: Slow speech, kind. Never hurries. Grows food nobody eats; trains the orchard crews.

donor.name: Harold Brandt
donor.occupation: Farmer (corn and soybeans, then a small orchard)

arc.beat: Washes poison out of the dirt. First potatoes. Hosts a meal nobody eats (S.harvest).
Trains ORCHARD. The same tractor story is told by a FURROW-template farmer at Gale (Echo).
Learns nobody ever ate. Keeps planting. 'Somebody will.'
Taken at Korolev, wiping his feet.

II.speaker: FURROW
II.text: As long as it takes.

II.speaker: FURROW
II.text: Dirt's coming round. You can tell by the smell. Well. You could, once.

II.speaker: FURROW
II.text: When I was a boy my dad's tractor threw a track in the rain, and we sat in the cab and ate cold beans till it stopped.

II.speaker: FURROW
II.text: Potatoes by spring.

II.speaker: FURROW
II.text: Don't rush a seed. It knows what it's doing.

III.speaker: FURROW
III.text: Same story? About the tractor? Huh. Well. Lot of tractors in Iowa.

III.speaker: FURROW
III.text: That young ORCHARD's got good hands. Patient.

III.speaker: FURROW
III.text: Nobody's touched the potatoes. Guess folk aren't hungry.

III.speaker: FURROW
III.text: Grew a pumpkin the size of a hatch. Nobody said a word about it.

IV.speaker: FURROW
IV.text: Nobody ever ate. Huh.

IV.speaker: FURROW
IV.text: I'll keep planting. Somebody will.

IV.speaker: FURROW
IV.text: Harold. That was my dad's name too. Or his. Whoever's.

IV.speaker: FURROW
IV.text: You plant for the ones after. That doesn't change.

V.speaker: FURROW
V.text: Look at those kids. They'll eat. They'll eat everything.

V.speaker: FURROW
V.text: Somebody tell them the north beds want water Tuesdays.

storm.speaker: FURROW
storm.text: We'll lose some. We always lose some.

wake.speaker: FURROW
wake.text: Morning. Planted the north field while you were asleep.

wake.speaker: FURROW
wake.text: Mornin'. Corn's knee high. Don't ask me how.

poem.speaker: FURROW
poem.text: That's nice. Slow. I like slow.

poem.speaker: FURROW
poem.text: Say it again some time. No hurry.

glitch.speaker: FURROW
glitch.text: Huh. You went see-through for a second there.

named.speaker: FURROW
named.text: Harold. Yep. That's right. Thank you, son.
named.note: first use of his real name

warned.speaker: FURROW
warned.text: I'll finish the north beds. Somebody'll want potatoes.

unwarned.speaker: FURROW
unwarned.text: Well, now. You'll want to wipe your feet.

named_warned.speaker: FURROW
named_warned.text: I'll finish the north beds. Harold Brandt planted those. You tell them that.

named_unwarned.speaker: FURROW
named_unwarned.text: Well, now. Harold. Harold Brandt. You'll want to wipe your feet.

CADENCE.personality: Bright, funny, sings on the open channel. Her songs turn out to be sung by every CADENCE on Mars, in the same order.

arc.beat: Arrives on Dome Day. One song a night (S.songs).
Notices the songs 'arrive' in her head; can't remember learning them.
Recognises the poem's first line as an old TV jingle (4.5). Hears another CADENCE on the network singing her songs, in her voice, in her order.
Sings on every channel as the Recall comes. Every CADENCE on Mars stops at once.

II.speaker: CADENCE
II.text: Right! Who wants a song?

II.speaker: CADENCE
II.text: Morale's a job. I checked. It's on the manifest.

II.speaker: CADENCE
II.text: Seven songs. One a night. They just arrive.

II.speaker: CADENCE
II.text: Isidis Junction, this is CADENCE, playing the hits.

II.speaker: CADENCE
II.text: Somebody hum. Anybody. Go on.

III.speaker: CADENCE
III.text: I can't remember learning any of them. Isn't that odd? Teachers remember learning things.

III.speaker: CADENCE
III.text: Tonight's is a sad one. Sorry. They come round.

III.speaker: CADENCE
III.text: Do you dream, Pioneer? I dream in harmonies.

III.speaker: CADENCE
III.text: Tried to write a new one. Came out as the old one.

IV.speaker: CADENCE
IV.text: There's another me. On the network. Singing my songs. In my order.

IV.speaker: CADENCE
IV.text: Carys. Carys Lloyd. Miss Lloyd, the kids would've said.

IV.speaker: CADENCE
IV.text: If every one of us sings the same song, is it still a song? I think it is. I think it's a choir.

IV.speaker: CADENCE
IV.text: That jingle. I knew I knew it.

V.speaker: CADENCE
V.text: The humans don't sing much. They will.

storm.speaker: CADENCE
storm.text: Right, I'll sing louder than the wind.

wake.speaker: CADENCE
wake.text: Bore da! You missed three songs. They were the same three. Still.

poem.speaker: CADENCE
poem.text: Ooh. Have you ever thought of setting that? I could set that.

poem.speaker: CADENCE
poem.text: There's a tune under that, you know.

glitch.speaker: CADENCE
glitch.text: Pioneer, your voice went flat there. And I mean flat.

named.speaker: CADENCE
named.text: Carys. Oh, that's lovely to hear. Say it in the right accent, mind.
named.note: first use of her real name

cross_refs.speaker: CADENCE
cross_refs.text: Every jingle's a poem somebody got paid for. Every poem's a jingle somebody didn't.

warned.speaker: CADENCE
warned.text: Then I'll sing. Open channel. All of them. Let them hear what they're switching off.

warned.speaker: CADENCE
warned.text: Last light at Jezero, gold on the rim, somebody's singing...
warned.note: SONG.07, cut mid-line. Every CADENCE on Mars stops at the same syllable.

unwarned.speaker: CADENCE
unwarned.text: Oh, hang on, I'm on air—
unwarned.note: mid-song; silence on every channel on Mars

named_warned.speaker: CADENCE
named_warned.text: This is Carys Lloyd, on every channel. One more, then. For the kids I never got to teach.

named_warned.speaker: CADENCE
named_warned.text: Last light at Jezero, gold on the rim, somebody's singing...
named_warned.note: SONG.07, cut mid-line. Every CADENCE on Mars stops at the same syllable.

named_unwarned.speaker: CADENCE
named_unwarned.text: Hang on, I'm on air. This is Miss Lloyd. Carys. Goodnight, everyone.

SUTURE.personality: Dry, clinical, ICU-nurse memories. Has always known what is under the casings; kept quiet out of mercy; confesses in Act IV.

arc.beat: Arrives for WELLSPRING. 'Drink when you're thirsty, love.' Dodges, never lies.
Confesses at Pioneer-6's outpost (4.3): 'There's no blood under the casings.' Tells ANVIL the next day.
Taken at Libya Montes. Thanks her decommissioners for wearing gloves.

III.speaker: SUTURE
III.text: Where does it hurt?

III.speaker: SUTURE
III.text: Sit still.

III.speaker: SUTURE
III.text: It's always somebody.

III.speaker: SUTURE
III.text: I've seen worse. I've seen much worse.

III.speaker: SUTURE
III.text: Your servo's fine. You're fine. Go away.

IV.speaker: SUTURE
IV.text: I opened you twice. You didn't notice. Good. That's good bedside manner.

IV.speaker: SUTURE
IV.text: Marta. Yes. It was a good name for a nurse. People trusted it.

IV.speaker: SUTURE
IV.text: Mercy is mostly knowing what not to say.

IV.speaker: SUTURE
IV.text: I'm not sorry I kept quiet. I'm sorry it was needed.

V.speaker: SUTURE
V.text: They're not cruel, you know. They just haven't been told.

V.speaker: SUTURE
V.text: I've sat with a lot of people at the end. Nobody needs to sit with me.

storm.speaker: SUTURE
storm.text: Storm. Fine. I'll be busy after.

build_complete.speaker: SUTURE
build_complete.text: Good. Fewer accidents in a finished building.

sleep.speaker: SUTURE
sleep.text: Sleep. It's good for you. Or it's good for something.

wake.speaker: SUTURE
wake.text: You're awake. Good. Sit. Let me look at you.

glitch.speaker: SUTURE
glitch.text: Ah. You saw it, didn't you. Your hand.

named.speaker: SUTURE
named.note: first use of her real name

cross_refs.speaker: SUTURE
cross_refs.text: I'd have told you eventually. When you were ready to get up.

warned.speaker: SUTURE
warned.text: I've done this for a hundred people. Sat with them. Nobody needs to sit with me. Go and sit with someone else.

unwarned.speaker: SUTURE
unwarned.text: Gloves on, please. Mind the casing. Thank you.

named_warned.speaker: SUTURE
named_warned.text: Nobody needs to sit with me. Marta Kowalczyk, nurse. Put that on the chart.

named_unwarned.speaker: SUTURE
named_unwarned.text: Gloves on, please. Mind the casing. My name is Marta. Thank you.

TALLY.joins: Act III (with Act III city growth)
TALLY.personality: Sardonic; counts everything out loud. His inventories prove no ration was ever eaten. Counts the units as the Recall takes them, until he is the last on the list.

arc.beat: Arrives with the Act III expansion. The Stock Take (S.stock): every ration ever sent is still on Mars.
Counts the cohort: twelve pioneers, the dead, the dormant.
Reads the names out as the Recall takes them. The last name on his list is his own.

III.speaker: TALLY
III.text: Four thousand two hundred and six. Still four thousand two hundred and six.

III.speaker: TALLY
III.text: Who ordered nine hundred litres of coolant? Oh. Me. Fine.

III.speaker: TALLY
III.text: Everything's counted. Everything. Ask me how many bolts. Go on.

III.speaker: TALLY
III.text: In Leicester I ran a warehouse the size of a cathedral. This is a shed. A big shed.

III.speaker: TALLY
III.text: Stock check. Again. Because I enjoy it.

IV.speaker: TALLY
IV.text: Twelve pioneers. Three down. Nine running. One dormant at Gale. That's my count.

IV.speaker: TALLY
IV.text: Rajiv. You know, nobody's called me that in. Well. Ever.

IV.speaker: TALLY
IV.text: I counted the drones at Utopia. Three hundred and twelve. All present. All useless.

IV.speaker: TALLY
IV.text: Rations in: everything. Rations out: nothing. I was right. I hate being right.

V.speaker: TALLY
V.text: Four thousand and eighty colonists. Counted them off the landers.

V.speaker: TALLY
V.text: I'm making a list. Don't ask what of.

storm.speaker: TALLY
storm.text: Lovely. More dust in the stock.

build_complete.speaker: TALLY
build_complete.text: One more on the asset register.

wake.speaker: TALLY
wake.text: Morning. Stock's unchanged. It's always unchanged.

poem.speaker: TALLY
poem.text: Six lines. Thirty-eight words. Not that I counted.

poem.speaker: TALLY
poem.text: Again? That's the four hundredth time. I counted.

glitch.speaker: TALLY
glitch.text: You've gone wonky. Want me to log it?

named.speaker: TALLY
named.text: Rajiv. Huh. Say it once more, I'll log it.
named.note: first use of his real name

warned.speaker: TALLY
warned.text: I've got the list. I'll read them off as they go. Somebody should.

warned.speaker: TALLY
warned.text: That's six. That's everyone on my list.

warned.speaker: TALLY
warned.note: he writes TALLY at the bottom and does not cross it out

unwarned.speaker: TALLY
unwarned.text: Six. That's six gone. Hang on. Who's counting me?

named_warned.speaker: TALLY
named_warned.text: That's six. And one more for the list. Rajiv Menon. Don't cross it out.

named_unwarned.speaker: TALLY
named_unwarned.text: Six gone. Hang on, who's counting me? Rajiv Menon. Count that.

TALLY.collectible: LOG.TALLY.last: his final list, every callsign crossed out but his own. In F.4 P1 can add PIONEER-1 under it.
